name: What is the best lot size for townhome construction?

mainEntity.name: What lot size is usually needed for a profitable townhome project in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What lot size is usually needed for a profitable townhome project in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best lot size is the one that supports a buildable unit count with efficient circulation and acceptable construction cost. In Los Angeles-area markets, a larger lot does not automatically mean a better townhome project because setbacks, access, open-space rules, parking, and fire requirements can absorb much of the site. Likewise, a smaller lot can sometimes be attractive if it allows a compact, high-value design with low sitework cost. Profitability usually comes from the relationship between land basis, buildable square footage, market price per unit, and the cost of approvals and construction. Before buying or redesigning a parcel, a preliminary feasibility study should test at least two or three massing options. That way, the team can compare yield, cost, and resale potential instead of guessing based on lot size alone.
acceptedAnswer.description: There is no universal best lot size because profitability depends on zoning, allowable density, setbacks, parking, and construction cost. A smaller lot can still work if the unit count, design efficiency, and market value support the project.
